claims: The Artemis II mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II mission splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission splashed down at 5:07 p.m. PDT on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean west of San Diego, California.
The Orion capsule carried four astronauts.
The Orion capsule returned after a 10-day mission.
The Orion capsule's reentry occurred at approximately 24,000 miles per hour.
The Artemis II mission lasted over 9 days.
Recovery teams were on-site immediately to secure the capsule and assist the crew, as shown on Fox News and reported by Florida Today.
The Artemis II mission was the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
